assessment_summary: I validated the installation performed via the guide's documented Docker method (`docker compose -f docker-compose.yml up --build`). I inspected the running environment (compose status, container health, ports, env config, database) and exercised the software's runtime behavior through its documented HTTP interfaces rather than relying on file existence. All three expected containers are up and healthy. The documented endpoints all respond: /health 200, /api (Swagger UI) 200, /api-json 200 with a complete OpenAPI document, /v2/topics 200 with real topic metadata, and /metrics 200. Functional POST tests returned real geospatial results (intersect and within returned Dresden/Sachsen features; nearestNeighbour returned a feature with computed __dist; transformGeoJSONToEsriJSON returned valid EsriJSON), and invalid payloads produced structured 400 validation errors, confirming the OpenAPI validator is active. The PostgreSQL/PostGIS database is provisioned with the sample data dump (schema ga with 15 tables; postgis/postgis_raster/postgis_topology extensions installed; non-empty test rows). pgAdmin responds with a 302 login redirect. The only limitation is that the host shell has no Node.js/pnpm, so validation was performed against the running Dockerized service, which is exactly the installation method the guide documents; this does not indicate any defect. The one deviation noted in the summary (creating .env.dev from .env.dev.sample) follows the guide's own instructions and is already resolved, with the app running healthy and RestartCount=0. Based on this objective evidence I assess the installation as complete and operational.
